root_cause.text: `handle_one_ule_extension()` in `drivers/media/dvb-core/dvb_net.c` used a network-controlled 8-bit `htype` value as an index into the `ule_mandatory_ext_handlers[]` and `ule_optional_ext_handlers[]` function-pointer tables even though those arrays only had 255 valid entries, allowing an out-of-bounds read and potential indirect call when `htype == 255`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (htype >= ARRAY_SIZE(ule_mandatory_ext_handlers)) return -1;` before either table is accessed, and the CVE text states that `htype` comes from `(ule_sndu_type & 0x00FF)` which can produce 255 while the tables have valid indices only `0-254`.
